title: Composition of multiplicative isogenies has finite central multiplicative kernel
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H_0,H_1,H_2$ be smooth connected affine $F$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme]. If $f:H_0\to H_1$ and $g:H_1\to H_2$ are multiplicative isogenies, then $g\circ f:H_0\to H_2$ is a multiplicative isogeny with central kernel. A multiplicative isogeny means a homomorphism whose pullback on coordinate algebras is faithfully flat and whose scheme-theoretic kernel is finite and of multiplicative type. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. Finite means having finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. A finite group scheme is of multiplicative type if, after extension to an algebraic closure, it is diagonalizable: it is isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, with comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ on the group-algebra basis. Central means commuting with every group element after every scalar extension.

source.place: Proposition 18.2 and its displayed exact sequence of kernels, printed p.387; Corollary 12.41, printed p.244; Corollary 12.22, printed p.239. The conjugation action is trivial by 12.41, not by finiteness of geometric points.

proof.text: Put $N=\ker f$, $Q=\ker g$, and $K=\ker(g\circ f)$. The kernel-subgroup statement makes these closed group schemes. The kernel fibre-product definition gives $K=H_0\times_{H_1}Q$ and a homomorphism $q:K\to Q$ induced by $f$, with kernel $N$. Indeed, on every $F$-algebra $A$, $x\in K(A)$ precisely when $f(x)\in Q(A)$, and $q(x)=1$ precisely when $f(x)=1$. These identifications are natural in $A$, and their inverse maps are the evident inclusion and projection. Conjugation by $H_0$ preserves $K$ and $N$, since homomorphisms send $hxh^{-1}$ to the conjugate of the image of $x$. Being closed subschemes of affine finite-type groups, these kernels are affine and of finite type.

source.place: Proposition 18.2, displayed kernel sequence; Exercise 5-8, p.123: direct kernel computation in the faithfully flat case.

proof.text: Write $A=F[H_1]$, $C=F[H_0]$, $B=F[Q]$ and $D=F[K]$. The affine fibre-product formula gives $D=B\otimes_A C$. Faithfully flat base change applied to $A\to C$ shows that $B\to D$ is faithfully flat. Thus $q$ is exactly a faithfully flat quotient with scheme-theoretic kernel $N$; the sequence $1\to N\to K\xrightarrow{q}Q\to1$ has the quotient hypothesis required by both extension lemmas below.

source.place: Proposition 18.2, displayed exact kernel sequence; affine faithfully-flat base change. Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00HQ and schemes.tex affine fibre-product construction.

proof.text: First establish the extra centrality required by the corrected extension-action lemma. Restrict conjugation to $H_0\times_F N\to N$, possible by Step 1. This is an action by group automorphisms, $H_0$ is smooth and connected, and $N$ is of multiplicative type by the hypothesis on $f$. Apply connected-action rigidity for groups of multiplicative type to obtain $hnh^{-1}=n$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $h\in H_0(A)$ and $n\in N(A)$. Thus $N$ is central in $H_0$, and restricting $h$ to $K(A)$ proves that $N$ is central in $K$. This uses no smoothness of $N$; in particular it applies to $\mu_p$ in characteristic $p$.

source.place: Corollaries 12.37 and 12.38, printed p.244; this supplies the central-subgroup hypothesis of Corollary 12.41 corrected in the Chapter 12 errata.

proof.text: The conjugation action $H_0\times_F K\to K$ is by group automorphisms and preserves $N$ by Step 1. By Step 3, $N$ is central in $K$. Apply corrected multiplicative-extension action rigidity with acting group $G=H_0$, middle group $E=K$, quotient $Q$, and quotient map $q$. The end groups $N,Q$ are of multiplicative type by the hypotheses on $f,g$, and $H_0$ is smooth and connected by hypothesis. Hence $hxh^{-1}=x$ for every $F$-algebra and all its $H_0$- and $K$-points. This is the asserted scheme-theoretic centrality of $K$ in $H_0$.

source.place: Proposition 18.2, application of Corollary 12.41, p.244, with its Chapter 12 erratum: N central in the middle group, verified in Step 3.

proof.text: Taking $h$ also in $K$ in the preceding identity proves that $K$ is commutative. Apply the commutative-extension lemma to $q:K\to Q$ from Step 2 and $N=\ker q$: its two end groups are of multiplicative type, and its middle group is now commutative. Therefore $K$ is of multiplicative type. This application does not assume that the finite kernel is smooth or connected.

To check finiteness scheme-theoretically, retain $B=F[Q]$ and $D=F[K]$ and put $P=F[N]$. There is an isomorphism $N\times_F K\simeq K\times_Q K$ given on all algebra points by $(n,x)\mapsto(nx,x)$; its inverse is $(y,x)\mapsto(yx^{-1},x)$, since $q(y)=q(x)$. Multiplication and inverse are morphisms, so these are inverse scheme maps. The affine fibre-product formula identifies this with a $D$-linear isomorphism $D\otimes_B D\simeq D\otimes_F P$, using the second projection on each side and swapping tensor factors where needed. If $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ is an $F$-basis of the finite-dimensional algebra $P$, then $1\otimes p_i$ generate $D\otimes_F P$ over $D$. Apply faithfully-flat finite-module descent to $B\to D$ of Step 2 and the $B$-module $D$. It follows that $D$ is finite over $B$. As $B$ is finite-dimensional over $F$, products of finite $B$-module generators of $D$ with an $F$-basis of $B$ span $D$ over $F$. Thus $K$ is finite, including when $N$ or $Q$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Proposition 18.2, finiteness of the composite kernel, expanded using the torsor identity of Lemma 5.24, p.104, and Stacks algebra.tex Tag 03C4(1), lemma-descend-properties-modules.

proof.text: Finally, extension of scalars along $F[H_2]\to F[H_0]$ is the composite of extension along $g^*$ and $f^*$: the tensor associativity map sends $c\otimes(a\otimes m)$ to $cf^*(a)\otimes m$, with inverse $c\otimes m\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes m)$. The two extension functors are exact and detect zero modules, so their composite is exact and detects zero modules. Therefore $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$ is faithfully flat. Together with the finiteness and multiplicative type of $K$ and its centrality, this proves every clause of the item.

source.place: Proposition 18.2: composition is faithfully flat by the tensor definition of faithful flatness; conclusion.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 18.2, printed p.387, using Corollaries 12.37--12.38 to supply the centrality hypothesis in corrected Corollary 12.41, then Corollary 12.22; kernel, tensor and finiteness calculations expanded.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q146-c9739baa0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This re-delivery repairs both points of the earlier E2/E7 return (40b90d08).

New nodes:
- lem-sfb-multiplicative-extension-action-rigidity now requires N central in E. This matches the Milne iAG erratum at the end of the PDF ('*p.244. In 12.41, N should be a central subgroup of H'). The report has a Source error section with the O(2) = G_m⋊C_2 counterexample, which I checked: conjugating (1,σ) by s gives (s²,σ). I proved the corrected statement myself: φ(g,x) = x⁻¹a(g,x) gives homomorphisms Q→N, which are constant by 12.36.
- lem-sfb-connected-action-multiplicative-type-rigidity is Milne 12.37 (p.244), specialised to smooth connected G over an algebraically closed F with D = D(M). It covers μ_p in characteristic p, where Aut(μ_p) is constant. lem-sfb-connected-action-torus-rigidity covers only tori, so the new node is not a duplicate. An rg -L search for 'multiplicative type|diagonalizable' found no other duplicate.
- lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-type-extension (Milne 12.22, p.239, sufficient direction) is true. I tested it on μ_p→μ_{p²}→μ_p.

Item steps:
- Step 1: kernels, from lem-sc-kernel-subgroup. Elementary.
- Step 2: F[K] = F[Q]⊗F[H1]F[H0], so q is faithfully flat by base change.
- Step 3 (new): N is central in H0 by rigidity, which is Milne 12.38, hence central in K.
- Step 4: the corrected 12.41 node gives K central in H0. I checked every hypothesis.
- Step 5: K is commutative, so 12.22 gives multiplicative type.
- Step 6: the torsor N×K ≅ K×_Q K plus finite-module descent along B→D makes K finite. The tensor sides match the descent statement.
- Step 7: a composite of faithfully flat maps is faithfully flat. Elementary.

The item statement is unchanged and agrees with Milne Def. 18.1 and Prop. 18.2 (p.387). proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. There is no cycle and no SGA citation. I accept the tool_use of lem-sc-kernel-subgroup. No re-split note applies to this item. I wrote no fixes; details are in review.md.
